title: Anomaly detection
summary: Anomaly detection identifies rare observations that deviate from normal behavior in a dataset. It is used across domains such as cybersecurity, finance, medicine, and fraud prevention. Techniques are categorized as supervised, semi-supervised, or unsupervised, with unsupervised methods being most common due to the lack of labeled data. Anomalies are scored numerically and converted to binary labels via a decision threshold. The field distinguishes point anomalies, contextual anomalies dependent on circumstances, and collective anomalies arising from related patterns. Historically rooted in intrusion detection, it now underpins fraud detection and system health monitoring, where anomalies may represent valid events or measurement errors depending on context.

mechanisms.title: Model-based normality assessment
mechanisms.explanation: Semi-supervised techniques construct a model of normal behavior from labeled training data, then test the likelihood of test instances being generated by that model. This approach assumes some portion of data is labeled and is used when normal patterns can be reliably captured.

mechanisms.title: Unsupervised pattern deviation
mechanisms.explanation: Unsupervised techniques assume data is unlabelled and detect anomalies by identifying observations that depart significantly from the majority of the data. These are the most commonly used methods due to their wider applicability where labeled normal and abnormal data are unavailable.
